status: Called in by Secretary of State
decision_conditions:
TREE WORKS (COMPLIANCE):  All tree work shall be carried out in accordance with British Standard BS3998 - Recommendations for Tree Work.  In addition: 
a)   No fires shall be lit within [10] metres of the nearest point of the canopy of any retained tree.  No equipment, machinery or structure shall be attached to or supported by a retained tree.
b)   No mixing of cement or use of other contaminating materials or substances shall take place within, or close enough to, a root protection area that seepage or displacement could cause them to enter a root protection area. 
c)   No alterations or variations to the approved works or tree protection schemes shall be made without prior written consent of the local planning authority.

REASON:  In the interest of the protection of trees and to safeguard visual amenities.
description:
(T2) Lime tree (Tilia x europaea)

This tree is in reasonable health but has not been reduced since 2022.

As it gets bigger it grows into the horse Chestnut and into the pavement.

In keeping with good arboricultural management and maintaining a works schedule, requested works are;

Reduce by up to 3 metres, back to previous points of reduction.


(T3) Horse Chestnut (Aesculus hippocastanum)

This very large tree is in good health but has not been reduced since 2020.

This tree is very close to the property so it is prudent to maintain the crowns size.

In keeping with good arboricultural management and maintaining a works schedule , requested works are;

Reduce crown by up to 2 metres back to previous points of reduction, leaving furnishing growth.


(T4) Sycamore (Acer pseudoplatanus)

This tree is not in the best health, and has not been reduced since 2022.

This tree has poor form and many cavities and has responded well to pruning in the past.

In keeping with good arboricultural management and maintaining a works schedule, requested works are;

Reduce crown by between 1.0 - 1.5 metres back past previous points of reduction, to remove dead tops. Reduce back to appropriate growth points.

Reduce lowest lateral branch over the road by 2 metres to reduce weight.
